title: Etale polynomial solutions are invariant under local maps of strictly henselian rings
statement:
Let $R,S$ be commutative strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $\theta:R\to S$ be a local ring homomorphism, meaning that $\theta(r)$ is a unit if and only if $r$ is a unit. Let $n\geq0$ and $P_1,\ldots,P_n\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $D=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(P_1,\ldots,P_n)$ and assume that the structural morphism $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $P_i^\theta\in S[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ for the polynomials obtained by applying $\theta$ to all coefficients. Then the coordinatewise map $(r_j)_j\mapsto(\theta(r_j))_j$ induces a bijection
$$\{r\in R^n:P_i(r)=0\text{ for every }i\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\{s\in S^n:P_i^\theta(s)=0\text{ for every }i\}.$$

source.place: Tag 04GX (lemma-strictly-henselian-solutions), both displayed solution sets and the coordinatewise bijection

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and $K=S/\mathfrak m_S$. Locality gives $\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, hence an injective field map $\bar\theta:k\to K$ and $q_S\theta=\bar\theta q_R$, where $q_R,q_S$ are the residue maps. For any commutative $R$-algebra $T$, evaluation identifies the solutions in $T^n$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,T)$: by the polynomial universal property an evaluation factors through $D$ exactly when it kills all $P_i$, and its values on the variable classes determine it. For $T=S$ these are precisely the equations $P_i^\theta=0$. Under these identifications the required map is $f\mapsto\theta f$.

source.place: Tag 04GX, first proof sentence; polynomial evaluation and passage to the quotient

proof.text: Let $E=S\otimes_R D$ and $C=k\otimes_R D$. Both are etale over their respective bases by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-target-etale-maps] first with base $R$, source algebra $D$, target $R$, then with base $S$, source algebra $E$, target $S$. In each application the target is module-finite (generated by $1$) and formally unramified over the base: there is at most one base-algebra map from the base itself into any algebra. It is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Thus reduction gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,S)\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(K\otimes_S E,K)$. The tensor universal property identifies the second bijection with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,S)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,K)$: extend $g:D\to S$ by $s\otimes d\mapsto s g(d)$, and extend $h:D\to K$ by $a\otimes(s\otimes d)\mapsto a q_S(s)h(d)$. The inverse operations restrict to $1\otimes d$. Similarly $\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,k)$ by $a\otimes d\mapsto a h(d)$.

source.place: Tag 04GX, second and third proof sentences, using Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), condition (8); Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale), base-change clause

proof.text: The etale $k$-algebra $C$ is a finite product $\prod_{i\in I}L_i$ of finite separable field extensions of $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. The field $k$ is separably closed by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. By the equivalent finite-extension formulation in [def-kun-separably-closed], each structural embedding $k\to L_i$ is an isomorphism. Consequently choose a $k$-algebra isomorphism $C\cong k^I$ with $I$ finite, allowing $I=\varnothing$.

For either field $F=k$ or $F=K$ (with its specified $k$-structure), every $k$-algebra map $k^I\to F$ is a coordinate projection followed by $k\to F$. Indeed the standard idempotents $e_i$ have sum $1$ and are pairwise orthogonal. Their images in a field are $0$ or $1$, exactly one being $1$; and $\sum_i a_i e_i$ therefore maps to the image of that coordinate $a_i$. Conversely each coordinate gives such a map. If $I$ is empty, the source is the zero ring and neither field admits a unital map from it, so both Hom sets are empty. Postcomposition by $\bar\theta$ preserves the coordinate label, hence is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k)\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,K)$. Restriction to $1\otimes d$ identifies the latter set with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,K)$, with inverse $h\mapsto(a\otimes d\mapsto\bar\theta(a)h(d))$.

source.place: Tag 04GX, last finite-product and scalar-extension sentences, with the coordinate argument expanded

proof.text: The square with top row $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,R)\xrightarrow{\theta\circ -}\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,S)$, bottom row $\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,k)\xrightarrow{\bar\theta\circ -}\operatorname{Hom}_R(D,K)$, and vertical residue maps commutes: at $d\in D$ the two composites are $q_S(\theta(f(d)))=\bar\theta(q_R(f(d)))$. Both vertical arrows are bijections by step 2 and the bottom arrow by steps 3--4. Their inverse-composite expression proves the top arrow bijective. Evaluating on the variable classes recovers exactly the coordinatewise map in the statement. When $n=0$, $D=R$ and both solution sets are singletons, consistently with this argument.

source.place: Tag 04GX, conclusion of the proof; explicit naturality of the reduction square

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-bbd34b9dc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and wrote review.md; no fixes. It is one commit that splits the item's proof into 5 steps, with the statement unchanged and no new nodes. Statement: it agrees with Stacks 04GX (algebra.tex:42635) hypothesis by hypothesis (local map of strictly henselian rings, n polynomials in n variables, D étale, coordinatewise bijection). Steps: they follow the Stacks proof sentence by sentence. Step 1 identifies solutions with Hom_R(D,T) via the polynomial universal property, and locality gives an injective residue map θ̄ with q_Sθ=θ̄q_R. Step 2 applies lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-target-etale-maps twice, each time with target equal to base: once to (R,D,R) and once to (S,S⊗D,S). The node's hypotheses hold: the target is module-finite, formally unramified over itself and henselian. The step never uses S as a target over R, which need not be module-finite. Step 2's tensor identifications are written with their inverses; I rechecked that the vertical maps are q∘−. Step 3 uses the étale-over-field product leaf and def-kun-separably-closed (no finite separable extensions) to get C≅k^I. Step 4 is the explicit idempotent argument, including I empty. Step 5 is the commuting square, three sides of which are bijections. Edge cases checked: n=0, D=0, non-injective θ (R to its residue field), and x²−a over separably closed fields with p≠2. Duplicates: none; 04GX appears only in the item and its citers. No SGA citation. The declared tool use of the pbc local-target node (Stacks 04GG(8)/04GK, generic algebra) is accepted.
